newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus to reply to EU on Boeing merger.
newsitem.headline: Airbus to reply to EU on Boeing merger.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus said on Tuesday it will submit comments to the European Commission which is looking into competitive aspects of a planned merger between U.S. aerospace giants Boeing and McDonnell Douglas.
"We will make observations on aspects of commercial aircraft affecting Airbus Industrie," an Airbus spokesman said.

The European Commission's Official Journal published a note on Monday which asked interested third parties to file comments on the U.S. merger within 15 days. The Commission launched a full probe on March 13 on the Boeing-McDonnell deal which will create a group with $48 billion of annual sales.
An industry source said the merger move carries numerous concerns for European commercial aerospace interests.

Boeing Co, the undisputed leader in commercial jets with around 60 percent of the world market, stands to gain from McDonnell's government-funded military programmes by acquiring a wider technology base for the civil sector.
Boeing could draw on so-called "dual-use technology", systems which have both civilian and military applications, to build its airliners.
The state-financed technology could be viewed as a form of indirect subsidy for the commercial aircraft, the source said.

State support for the commercial aircraft business is a highly emotive issue between the United States and European authorities, with both sides attacking each other's practices despite a 1992 trade accord which left much dissatisfaction on both sides of the Atlantic.

Airbus' partners receive repayable launch aid, which U.S. competitors view as anti-competitive state support, whereas Europeans point to military-funded research and development contracts which lay the technology base for U.S. firms.
A major concern over a merged Boeing-McDonnell lies in the greater leverage the group would have in negotiating exclusive contracts with airlines, effectively locking out Airbus for 25 years.
This is a worry already voiced by European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, following all-Boeing deals agreed by Delta Air Lines and AMR Corp's American Airlines.

An enlarged Boeing could also bring pressure to bear on suppliers and subcontractors, the source said. However this a charge denied by Boeing chairman and chief executive Phil Condit, who has said it is in Boeing's interest to have strong suppliers with a broad business base.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
